text:
Appendix 11: Guidance on an Oil Spill Response Organisation's returns to Accrediting Bodies
This appendix provides guidance on the information that Oil Spill Response Organisations (OSROs) must submit to their accrediting body through Interim and Quarterly Returns. These returns help accrediting bodies monitor changes that may affect an Oil Spill Response Organisation's accreditation status, including changes to capability, operations, resources, personnel, contracts and client base.
The accrediting body may carry out an interim assessment based on information provided in an Interim Return or Quarterly Return.
Interim Returns
An Oil Spill Response Organisation (OSRO) must submit an Interim Return if there have been significant changes to its Capability Statement since its last accreditation or re-accreditation.
A significant change is a change in risk profile or client base that requires a substantial adjustment to resource levels or the way services are delivered. This may include, for example, the need to apply for accreditation in another response category.
The Interim Return must include details of:
- the change in client base
- any resulting changes to capability
The OSRO should submit the Interim Return to the accrediting body as soon as reasonably practicable following the change in circumstances.
Quarterly Returns
An OSRO must submit a Quarterly Return to its accrediting body by the last day of March, June, September and December each year.
The Quarterly Return should provide details of changes to administration, operations, contracts and any other matters relevant to the organisation’s accreditation.
This may include, but is not limited to:
- incidents responded to, including post-incident reports
- exercises conducted, including post-exercise reports
- evidence that lessons identified have been captured, tracked and acted upon
- changes to administrative details, including points of contact
- changes to contractual arrangements or insurance
- changes to procedures
- changes to response personnel, including recruitment and departures
- changes to equipment stockpiles, vessels, vehicles or premises
- changes to client base
- any other information relevant to the OSRO’s accreditation status
